glosses: To count (things or people) so as to add up and get a sum total.

examples.text: He counted up the glasses, and realized there were fifteen missing.

translations.source_sense_description: eine Sache mit einer oder mehreren anderen verrechnen

glosses: To add up; count up; compute the amount of; tally; come to an accounting of

examples.text: How many things are there which I ought to reckon up, that I have neglected; and how many others are there, which, if I did reckon them up, would overwhelm me with confusion. The grocer has given me a subject that I shall do well to pursue.

glosses: To harshly criticize.

examples.text: We reckoned him up pretty bad.

glosses: To perceive (reckon) (someone or something).

examples.text: I reckoned him up as a troublemaker at first glance.

glosses: To join or unite (e.g. one thing to another, or as several particulars) so as to increase the number, augment the quantity, or enlarge the magnitude, or so as to form into one aggregate.

glosses: To give by way of increased possession (to someone); to bestow (on).

examples.text: The Lord shall add to me another son.
Back to thy punishment, False fugitive, and to thy speed add wings.

glosses: To append (e.g. a statement); to say further information.

examples.text: He added that he would willingly consent to the entire abolition of the tax

examples.text: It adds to our anxiety.
